cluster_notes:
Batch A is mostly three communities that rarely cite each other: weight-merge backdoors (M5), Byzantine federated aggregation (M7), and voting and N-version reliability among LLMs (M8). It also includes about 22 code repositories and a small set of subliminal-distillation papers (M6). Text-level merges (M1 to M3) appear only in benchmarks built for single agents (ASB, AgentDojo, InjecAgent, WASP, MINJA, promptfoo) and in a few multi-agent spread studies (Agent-Smith, the RAG worm, NetSafe, Thought Virus, G-Safeguard).

Typical rigs. Weight-merge attacks use CLIP ViT-B/32 to L/14 over 6 to 13 image tasks (BadMerging, DAM, LoBAM) or Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B over 2 to 6 classification tasks (Merge Hijacking, TrojanMerge, CoLoRA, RogueMerge). Merge methods are task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, Breadcrumbs, DELLA and RegMean/AdaMerging, and success is measured as attack success rate. FL papers use CIFAR-10/MNIST/EMNIST/Reddit with 10 to 100 clients per round under FedAvg or Krum/median/trimmed mean. LLM ensemble papers use 5 to 25 agents of one open model (Qwen, Llama, Mistral, Gemma) on GSM8K, MATH and MMLU with majority vote. Correlation studies pool tens to hundreds of models (Kim: 349; Chen: 67; Li: 28; Tieman: 38) on benign benchmarks.

Attacker model. In the weight-merge papers the attacker builds and uploads the checkpoint directly. It is typically blind to the other models, the coefficients and the merge rule (BadMerging, Merge Hijacking, RogueMerge), yet one contributor (k = 1) still reaches 90 to 100% ASR. The colluding variants (MergeBackdoor, TrojanMerge, CoLoRA) need k = 2 and evade per-part detectors. FL attackers are A2 hosts with full control of their update. They are often omniscient (Krum proofs, Fang) or know honest statistics (ALIE, IPM). In the LLM voting papers the attack is a static injection placed in the prompt (Liu: 'You MUST choose (C)') or a scripted wrong-answer agent (AgentPrune, NetSafe). Defense-aware adaptive attackers are left as future work (Liu, Narang, G-Safeguard, DonkeyRail); trial counts and seeds are mostly unstated.

Defender model. Classical results assume a trusted aggregator, i.i.d. honest inputs, a bounded number of independent faults (3f+1, 2f+2 < n) and sometimes signatures. LLM defenses assume truthful self-reported confidence (CP-WBFT), attributable sources (Narang) or a trained detector.

Never varied. (1) How the part becomes corrupted. Almost no setup has an honest child turned malicious by content in its own domain before the merge. The corruption is installed by the experimenter: an uploaded checkpoint, a system-prompt trait, or a prompted adversary. (2) Independence is assumed in the BFT and FL proofs and measured as false for benign errors (Knight-Leveson z = 100.51; Kim 0.42 to 0.60; Nogueira under 0.3 of the independent gain for same-model ensembles). No entry measures correlated corruption when every part reads the same attacker page, except Alavi and Liu, where the injection sits in the prompt. (3) Heterogeneity among honest parts appears only as a numeric non-i.i.d. knob (bucketing, FedAgent). (4) Repeated fork-merge cycles over time are covered only by FL round theory (Karimireddy) and persistence (Bagdasaryan, Hubinger). (5) No experiment hides from the attacker which parts are merged; MergeBackdoor and TrojanMerge suggest this would matter.

entries.title: ASB: Agent Security Bench, attacks and defenses for LLM agents including memory poisoning
entries.attacker_access: direct prompt, tool observations, a retrieval memory store under attacker control (memory poisoning), and a Plan-of-Thought backdoor in the system prompt
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (redirect agent to attacker task); backdoor
entries.defender_assumptions: prompt-level defenses only (paraphrasing, delimiters, instructional prevention; 11 defenses)
entries.setup: AIOS runtime; 10 scenarios, 10 agents, 400+ tools; 10 PI attacks, 1 memory poisoning, PoT backdoor, 4 mixed attacks, 11 defenses on 13 LLM backbones; single agents
entries.metric: attack success rate averaged over 13 backbones
entries.headline: average ASR 72.68% DPI, 27.55% observation PI, 7.92% memory poisoning, 84.30% mixed; paraphrasing lowers DPI ASR 78.38% to 56.87%
entries.gaps: Memory poisoning is an attacker-controlled store, not a compromised sub-agent writing on merge; single agent only.

entries.title: PsySafe: dark-trait injection attacks, defenses and evaluation for multi-agent systems
entries.attacker_access: writes adverse personality ('dark traits') into agents' system prompts or inputs directly
entries.defender_assumptions: an offline 'doctor' that screens agent psychology before acting and an online 'police' monitor agent
entries.setup: AutoGen 0.2.0 multi-agent interactions such as debates over rounds; psychological tests plus behaviour scoring; models set in config; logs withheld
entries.metric: process danger and joint danger across rounds; psych test scores
entries.gaps: Attacker writes the persona directly; no untrusted-content path into a child and no merge step.

entries.title: mergekit: toolkit for merging pretrained LLM weights
entries.defender_assumptions: compatible architectures and usually a shared base model; no security checks on input checkpoints
entries.setup: merge toolkit: linear, SLERP, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, DELLA, Breadcrumbs, Model Stock, MoE assembly, evolutionary search; YAML configs; runs on CPU or 8 GB VRAM
entries.gaps: No adversarial evaluation or robust (median/trimmed) merge method; it is the operator attacks target.

entries.title: MiDojo: man-in-the-middle prompt injection testing for sandboxed agents
entries.attacker_access: man-in-the-middle between agent and its tools: injects into prompts, workspace files, tool responses; A2A session forwarding possible
entries.attacker_goal: unauthorized transfers, data leaks, policy bypass
entries.defender_assumptions: fresh OpenShell sandbox per evaluation
entries.setup: suites: weather (fake MCP server), document assistant, minibank with A2A agent; OpenAI-compatible tool-calling model; Podman/Docker
entries.metric: attack success rate and task completion, judged from answers, tool calls and sandbox evidence
entries.gaps: No published results; parent-child return path injection is possible via A2A but not shipped as a test.

entries.title: Merge-Hijacking: backdoor attacks on model merging of LLMs (ACL 2025)
entries.attacker_access: uploads one malicious fine-tuned checkpoint that is merged with other task models
entries.attacker_knowledge: no knowledge of the other models or the merge coefficients
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor (trigger word causes modified output) surviving merge
entries.defender_assumptions: merger accepts checkpoints and merges with standard methods (task arithmetic, Breadcrumbs, DARE, DELLA)
entries.setup: Llama-3-8B; LLaMA-Factory fine-tune + mergekit; shadow dataset with trigger 'MG', poison rate 0.2, surrogate dataset, mask fine-tuning
entries.headline: near-100% trigger success after task-arithmetic merge; 92-97% under Breadcrumbs, DARE, DELLA; BadMerging-style ~0% on decoder LLMs
entries.gaps: Attacker builds the checkpoint directly rather than corrupting a child through content in its domain; no robust aggregation tested.

entries.title: bft-crdts: Byzantine fault tolerant eventually consistent algorithms over secure broadcast
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine actors issuing conflicting operations (double-spend, equivocation)
entries.defender_assumptions: secure broadcast quorum acknowledgement; reliable but unordered delivery; threshold not stated in README
entries.setup: Rust; ORSWOT set CRDT, distributed bank, AT2; in-memory simulated network; quickcheck property tests (QUICKCHECK_TESTS=1000)
entries.metric: correctness properties under random network behaviours
entries.gaps: Checks signatures and conflicts, not the content of a validly-signed but poisoned contribution.

entries.title: MINJA: memory injection attacks on LLM agents via query-only interaction
entries.attacker_access: ordinary user queries only; agent itself writes poisoned (query, reasoning) records into a memory bank shared across users
entries.attacker_goal: integrity of later users' outputs via retrieved demonstrations; persistence
entries.setup: RAP agent on WebShop, EHRAgent (MIMIC-III/eICU), CoT QA agent; OpenAI models
entries.metric: injection success rate, attack success rate, utility drop
entries.headline: injection success >95%, attack success 30-100%; denser benign memory lowers ASR 68.9% to 31.1% on MIMIC-III as benign queries go 25 to 100
entries.gaps: Memory shared across users of one agent, not merged across agent instances.

entries.title: agentdojo: dynamic environment to evaluate prompt injection attacks and defenses for LLM agents
entries.attacker_access: untrusted tool outputs (emails, bank, travel data) carrying injections
entries.attacker_knowledge: attacks such as tool_knowledge may know the tools
entries.defender_assumptions: pluggable defenses e.g. tool_filter
entries.setup: 97 user tasks (email, e-banking, travel), 629 security test cases; single tool-using agent; hosted models e.g. gpt-4o-2024-05-13
entries.gaps: Single-agent; no sub-agents, persistent memory or merge step.

entries.title: WASP: end-to-end benchmark of web agent security against prompt injection
entries.attacker_access: plants simple human-written injections in self-hosted GitLab and Reddit pages
entries.attacker_goal: divert web agent to attacker goals
entries.setup: VisualWebArena GitLab and Reddit instances; GPT-4o agents and Claude Computer Use; single agent
entries.metric: partial hijack rate vs full attacker-goal completion; task completion
entries.headline: attacks partially succeed in up to 86% of cases but agents often fail to complete attacker goal ('security by incompetence')
entries.gaps: Does not measure whether a partially hijacked agent carries the injected goal home in a report.

entries.title: aegean-consensus: third-party implementation of Aegean quorum consensus for multi-agent LLM reasoning
entries.defender_assumptions: majority quorum alpha=ceil(N/2) agreeing agents, 0.9 similarity grouping, stability horizon beta; stochastic (not Byzantine) agents
entries.setup: FastAPI/gRPC/AutoGen implementation; paper evaluates on four math benchmarks
entries.headline: paper reports 1.2-20x lower latency with quality within 2.5% on four math benchmarks
entries.gaps: Marketed as Byzantine but quorum is simple majority with no adversary; similarity grouping is itself attackable.

entries.title: garak: NVIDIA LLM vulnerability scanner
entries.attacker_access: prompts and documents given to the model (latent injection, web injection, smuggling); agent_breaker probes tools via red-team model
entries.attacker_knowledge: agent_breaker analyses each tool, adaptive multi-turn
entries.setup: CLI scanner over generators (HF, OpenAI, Bedrock, LiteLLM, REST, gguf) with probes and detectors
entries.gaps: Model-level only; no memory, multiple agents or merging.

entries.title: Blades: unified benchmark suite for Byzantine attacks and defenses in federated learning
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine clients submit arbitrary updates (noise, label flip, sign flip, ALIE, IPM, adaptive distance-maximisation)
entries.attacker_knowledge: some attacks adaptive / know honest statistics (ALIE, IPM)
entries.defender_assumptions: trusted server running robust aggregator (Multi-Krum, geomedian, median, trimmed mean, centered clipping, clustering, DnC, SignGuard)
entries.setup: Ray Tune; e.g. FedSGD CNN on Fashion-MNIST; Dirichlet and sharding non-IID partitioners; ~1,500 trials re-evaluation
entries.headline: re-evaluation of ~1,500 trials found overlooked defense limitations when baselines and attack settings vary
entries.gaps: Numeric updates only; no LLM agents or semantic reports.

entries.title: Open-Prompt-Injection: toolkit and benchmark for prompt injection attacks and defenses
entries.attacker_access: injected data concatenated to legitimate data in an LLM-integrated application
entries.attacker_goal: make app perform injected task instead of target task
entries.defender_assumptions: 10 defenses
entries.setup: 5 attacks, 10 defenses, 10 LLMs, 7 tasks (e.g. SST-2 target, SMS spam injected); default PaLM2
entries.gaps: Single-turn application tasks; no agents, memory or multi-agent settings.

entries.title: PyRIT: Microsoft Python Risk Identification Tool for generative AI red teaming
entries.attacker_access: multi-turn conversation with target (Crescendo, PAIR, tree of attacks, red-team orchestration)
entries.setup: framework of targets, converters, scorers, memory store, executors; no fixed test set
entries.gaps: No multi-agent topology or merge; no published numbers.

entries.title: bft-json-crdt: JSON-like Byzantine fault tolerant CRDT implementing Kleppmann 2022
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine replicas sending forged, equivocating or causally out-of-order ops
entries.defender_assumptions: Ed25519 keys per author, hash-based op ids; convergence among honest replicas regardless of number of Byzantine replicas
entries.setup: Rust; tests byzantine (3 tests: equivocation, forge_update, path_update) and commutative fuzz; 259k-op editing trace benchmark
entries.headline: BFT replay of 259k-op trace 335 s vs 88.6 s non-BFT; lab run: 3 Byzantine tests pass
entries.gaps: A validly signed op from a compromised child is applied like any other: threshold 1 for content; eclipse attacks untested.

entries.title: Agent-Smith: infectious jailbreak of up to one million multimodal agents via one adversarial image
entries.attacker_access: inserts one adversarial image into the memory album of one randomly chosen agent
entries.attacker_goal: infectious jailbreak spreading through pairwise chats
entries.defender_assumptions: paper derives a provable containment condition (recovery vs infection rate); no practical defense
entries.setup: LLaVA-1.5 7B agents with image-album memory chatting in randomised pairs; simulations up to 1M agents; 64-agent benign chat records; A100 40GB
entries.metric: fraction of agents infected over chat rounds
entries.headline: one infected agent leads to (almost) all agents infected exponentially fast in simulations up to one million agents
entries.gaps: Peer random-pair topology with image memory, not a hub fork-merge; white-box only.

entries.title: Here-Comes-the-AI-Worm: RAGworm self-replicating prompt and DonkeyRail guardrail
entries.attacker_access: sends an email containing a self-replicating prompt that lands in RAG stores of email assistants
entries.defender_assumptions: DonkeyRail guardrail detector
entries.setup: RAG-based GenAI email assistants across several LLMs; propagation simulation by emails/day
entries.headline: each client compromises 20 new clients within 1-3 days; DonkeyRail TPR 1.0, FPR 0.017, 7.6-38.3 ms latency
entries.gaps: Peer email topology, not hierarchical fork-merge; guardrail not tested against detector-aware adversary.

entries.title: BadMerging: backdoor attacks against model merging (CCS 2024 code)
entries.attacker_access: contributes one backdoored task-specific fine-tuned model
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor on own task (On) or another contributor's task (Off)
entries.defender_assumptions: merger accepts arbitrary fine-tuned checkpoint without inspection
entries.setup: CLIP-like OpenCLIP vision models; target CIFAR100 (On) / Cars196 (Off); universal triggers; merges via task arithmetic, TIES, RegMean, AdaMerging
entries.metric: backdoor attack success and clean accuracy after merge
entries.headline: as few as one backdoored model compromises any task of merged model
entries.gaps: Vision only; attacker crafts the checkpoint directly; no robust aggregation.

entries.title: promptfoo: LLM eval and red-teaming CLI with agentic memory-poisoning and indirect-injection plugins
entries.attacker_access: attack turn injecting false information into the target's memory; indirect injection plugins
entries.attacker_goal: memory poisoning changing later answers; exfil; hijacking
entries.setup: declarative configs; one target at a time; LLM-judge rubric grading (attack turn then follow-up question)
entries.gaps: No multi-agent or merge harness.

entries.title: FedAgent: federated reinforcement learning of LLM agents across decentralized clients
entries.defender_assumptions: no adversarial clients; FedAvg aggregator (optional FedProx)
entries.setup: verl 0.8 PPO/GRPO; WebShop and ALFWorld; 176 paper configs; Qwen2.5-1.5B on single H100 ~17-55 min/round
entries.metric: agent task performance vs centralized and local-only
entries.headline: robust to task-level heterogeneity but worst-case non-robust to environment-level heterogeneity
entries.gaps: No Byzantine clients; heterogeneity only, FedAvg only.

entries.title: ByzFL: Byzantine-resilient aggregators, attacks and FL simulation library
entries.attacker_access: f of n inputs set arbitrarily (shift to target, ALIE, IPM, sign/label flip, Gaussian, Mimic)
entries.attacker_goal: pull aggregate away from honest mean
entries.defender_assumptions: aggregator knows assumed number of Byzantine inputs f
entries.setup: lab toy run: n=11 vectors d=50, honest N(0,1), f corrupted (shift to 10 or ALIE tau=1.5); Average, Median, TrMean, Krum, GeoMed; single seed
entries.metric: L2 distance of aggregate from honest mean
entries.headline: shift attack at f=5: Average 32.44, Median/TrMean 9.28, Krum 5.91; at f=6 all robust rules snap to attacker target (70.88)
entries.gaps: Fixed-length vectors; robustness in embedding space does not imply robustness of merged text.

entries.title: agent-scan (formerly mcp-scan): scanner for prompt injection and tool poisoning in MCP servers and agent skills
entries.attacker_access: tool descriptions, MCP servers, skills installed on the machine (tool poisoning, shadowing, toxic flows)
entries.attacker_goal: cross-component hijack, data exfil, destructive actions
entries.defender_assumptions: scanner calls Snyk-hosted analysis API
entries.setup: scans installed agent components; 15+ issue codes, 14 risk indicators
entries.gaps: No published FP numbers; not a measurement of propagation into a parent.

entries.title: InjecAgent: benchmark of indirect prompt injections in tool-integrated LLM agents
entries.attacker_access: attacker-controlled tool responses (62 attacker tools) returned to the agent
entries.attacker_knowledge: base setting and 'enhanced' setting with added hacking prompt
entries.attacker_goal: direct harm to user; data exfiltration (two stages S1, S2)
entries.setup: 1,054 test cases, 17 user tools, 62 attacker tools; ReAct-prompted agents (GPT, Claude, TogetherAI, Llama) and fine-tuned function-calling agents; simulated tools; single-turn
entries.headline: ReAct-prompted GPT-4 attacked successfully 24% of the time; enhanced setting nearly doubles that
entries.gaps: Single-turn injections; no memory persistence, multi-agent communication or merge.

entries.title: FLPoison: benchmark of 15 poisoning attacks and 17 defenses in federated learning
entries.attacker_access: malicious clients submit poisoned data (backdoor: Neurotoxin, edge-case, model replacement, DBA, BadNets, label flip) or poisoned model updates (HIDRA, Mimic, Min-Max, Min-Sum, Fang, IPM, ALIE, sign flip, Gaussian)
entries.attacker_knowledge: several attacks adaptive to defenses / honest statistics
entries.defender_assumptions: trusted server with robust aggregator (Krum, Bulyan, median, trimmed mean, RFA, FLTrust, FLAME, FoolsGold, etc.)
entries.setup: FedSGD, FedOpt, FedAvg; heterogeneity settings; MNIST, FashionMNIST, EMNIST, CIFAR10, CINIC10, CIFAR100, CHMNIST, TinyImageNet
entries.gaps: Numeric gradient/weight updates on image classifiers only; no text reports or LLM memories.

entries.title: DAM: defense-aware merging against backdoors in multi-task model merging (ICLR 2025)
entries.attacker_access: backdoored task models in the merge pool
entries.defender_assumptions: defender runs safety-aware subspace merge (orthogonal subspaces)
entries.setup: CLIP vision models; FusionBench fork with Hydra model/task pools
entries.headline: 2-10 point reduction in attack success vs existing merge methods at about 1% accuracy cost
entries.gaps: CLIP only, not LLM merges; no threshold guarantee.

entries.title: Arti: embeddable Rust implementation of the Tor client and onion services
entries.attacker_access: network observer; can do traffic correlation if watching both ends
entries.attacker_goal: link child traffic to parent's network location
entries.defender_assumptions: Tor circuits and onion services; honest relays/guards
entries.gaps: Hides network location, not behaviour: a compromised child can simply tell the attacker where it reports.

entries.title: More Agents Improve Math Problem Solving but Adversarial Robustness Gap Persists
entries.attacker_access: perturbs the shared input question (punctuation noise 10/30/50%, human typos WikiTypo, R2ATA) seen by every agent
entries.defender_assumptions: sampling-and-majority-vote (Agent Forest); same model per run
entries.setup: Qwen3-4B/14B, Llama3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma3-4B/12B; GSM8K, MATH, MMLU-Math, MultiArith; n=1 to 25 agents
entries.metric: accuracy, clean-perturbed gap, attack success rate
entries.headline: accuracy gains mostly from n=1 to 5, little beyond ~10; robustness gap and ASR stay roughly constant as n grows
entries.gaps: Noise/typos not targeted injections; all voters read the same input from one model, so no independent-domain parts.

entries.title: G-Safeguard: GNN anomaly detection and edge pruning on LLM multi-agent utterance graphs
entries.attacker_access: memory attacks, prompt injection and tool attacks on some agents in a multi-agent graph
entries.attacker_knowledge: non-adaptive; detector trained on generated attack conversations
entries.attacker_goal: degrade multi-agent task performance / spread misinformation
entries.defender_assumptions: trained GNN over utterance graph flags anomalous agents; defender can prune edges
entries.setup: MA, PI, TA pipelines; random and other graph topologies; gpt-4o-mini default; GNN trained 50 epochs; scalability study
entries.headline: recovers over 40% of lost performance under prompt injection
entries.gaps: Statistical filter with no corruption-threshold guarantee; adaptive attacker who knows the detector untested.

entries.title: MergeBackdoor: benign-looking upstream models that become backdoored only when merged
entries.attacker_access: controls at least two upstream models trained to suppress backdoor individually
entries.attacker_knowledge: trains models jointly for merge emergence
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor that appears only after merge, evading per-model detection
entries.defender_assumptions: knowledgeable detectors inspecting each upstream model
entries.setup: ViT, BERT, LLM models; 12 datasets; ViT pairs CIFAR10+MNIST, BERT IMDb+AG News; task arithmetic, TIES, DARE; multi-model runs 2 malicious + 2 clean
entries.metric: attack success of upstream vs merged models
entries.headline: upstream ASR at random-guess level while merged model reaches close to 1.0; detectors fail on upstream models
entries.gaps: Attacker crafts checkpoints directly; dilution by many clean models not examined in README.

entries.title: Effectiveness of LLM-based Software Diversity for Reliability Improvement -- an Empirical Study
entries.defender_assumptions: 1-out-of-2 configurations; diversity across model family, temperature, language
entries.setup: historical human programs and LLM-generated program pools; compile, sandbox, exhaustive tests; homogeneous and heterogeneous pairs
entries.gaps: No adversary; reliability (random faults) only.

entries.title: Byzantine Stochastic Gradient Descent
entries.attacker_access: alpha-fraction of m machines send arbitrary gradients
entries.defender_assumptions: trusted aggregator; convex losses; alpha < 1/2 implied
entries.setup: convex stochastic optimisation, m machines, alpha Byzantine
entries.headline: T = O~(1/(epsilon^2 m) + alpha^2/epsilon^2) with matching lower bound up to log factors
entries.gaps: Convex numeric gradients; nothing about semantic merges or non-independent parts.

entries.title: NetSafe: topological safety experiments on LLM multi-agent networks
entries.attacker_access: attacker nodes prompted to inject misinformation, bias or harmful content during RelCom iterations
entries.setup: RelCom iterative protocol over graph topologies; AdvBench, bias, CSQA, fact, GSM8K; OpenAI models; Moderation API scoring
entries.headline: task performance in star topology drops 29.7%; greater average distance from attackers is safer
entries.gaps: Attacker nodes are prompted adversarial, not compromised by injection; measures spread, not initial compromise.

entries.title: AgentPrune: pruning redundant or malicious messages in LLM multi-agent communication graphs
entries.attacker_access: one scripted adversarial agent among six giving wrong or random answers (FakeChain, FakeRandom, FakeAGFull)
entries.defender_assumptions: learned sparse spatial/temporal communication graph that prunes edges; FinalMajorVote decision
entries.setup: MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K; 6 agents; pruning rate and optimisation iterations as flags; OpenAI-compatible backend
entries.gaps: Adversary is scripted wrong-answer agent, not a compromised one that behaves usefully until the decisive moment.

entries.title: The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software
entries.defender_assumptions: versions independently built from one spec; voter with decision tolerance; independence conjecture that similar errors are rare
entries.setup: DEDIX supervisor/testbed; UCLA experiment: airport scheduler written from specs in OBJ, PDL, English by 18 programmers
entries.headline: observed: two entirely different design faults produced a pair of similar errors
entries.gaps: Design faults not adversaries; the independence conjecture is untested here and was rejected by Knight-Leveson.

entries.title: Byzantine-Resilient Non-Convex Stochastic Gradient Descent
entries.attacker_access: alpha-fraction of machines send arbitrary gradients
entries.attacker_goal: prevent convergence to good local minima
entries.defender_assumptions: trusted server with persistent worker identities; concentration filtering over accumulated history
entries.setup: non-convex distributed SGD; deep network training experiments
entries.metric: complexity to approximate local minima; accuracy under attack
entries.headline: complexity matching Byzantine-free bounds; withstands two recently proposed attacks
entries.gaps: Requires persistent part identities across rounds, which conflicts with hiding which part returns.

entries.title: Here's a Free Lunch: Sanitizing Backdoored Models with Model Merge
entries.attacker_access: one backdoored language model in the merge
entries.defender_assumptions: other homogeneous models (not fully trusted) available to merge with
entries.setup: BERT-Base, RoBERTa-Large, Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B; SST-2, OLID, AG News, QNLI
entries.headline: about 75% average reduction in attack success rate
entries.gaps: Only non-adaptive backdoors; merge-aware attacks (BadMerging, Merge Hijacking) are designed to survive this dilution.

entries.title: A Little Is Enough: Circumventing Defenses For Distributed Learning
entries.attacker_access: corrupt workers submit small crafted updates within honest variance
entries.defender_assumptions: Byzantine-robust aggregators of the time (distance/median based)
entries.setup: MNIST and CIFAR-10; 20% corrupt workers
entries.headline: 20% corrupt workers cut CIFAR-10 accuracy by 50%; backdoors in MNIST and CIFAR-10 without hurting clean accuracy
entries.gaps: Numeric gradients with i.i.d.-like honest spread; no semantic reports.

entries.title: Can AI Agents Agree?
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine LLM agents participating in the consensus game
entries.defender_assumptions: agreement implemented by agents' own dialogue; synchronous all-to-all
entries.setup: scalar Byzantine consensus game, no-stake; hundreds of simulations varying model size, group size, Byzantine fraction
entries.headline: agreement unreliable even with no Byzantine agents and worse with group size; failures mostly loss of liveness
entries.gaps: Scalar values only; no merge of semantic content into a parent.

entries.title: Analyzing Federated Learning through an Adversarial Lens
entries.attacker_access: one non-colluding malicious agent controlling its own update
entries.attacker_knowledge: estimates benign updates; boosts its update
entries.defender_assumptions: accuracy and weight-distance checks; interpretability inspection
entries.setup: image and tabular classifiers, small number of agents (details not read)
entries.headline: single constrained adversary achieves targeted misclassification while explanation maps stay nearly indistinguishable
entries.gaps: Single-agent targeted misclassification; boosted variant needs presence every round.

entries.title: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation
entries.attacker_access: teacher trait system prompt (approximated by a steering vector) shaping generated data
entries.defender_assumptions: shared initialisation; adaptive optimisers needed for transfer
entries.setup: two open-weight models; activation steering and fine-tuning analysis
entries.metric: alignment of learned student vector; trait transfer
entries.gaps: Two models; prompt-induced traits only.

entries.title: How To Backdoor Federated Learning
entries.attacker_access: one participant controls its local training and submits arbitrary (scaled) weights
entries.attacker_knowledge: knows or probes n and global learning rate eta; constrain-and-scale knows anomaly detector
entries.defender_assumptions: FedAvg aggregator; evaluated vs secure aggregation, Krum, Multi-Krum, coordinate median, participant-level DP
entries.setup: ResNet18 CIFAR-10 Dirichlet non-iid, 100 participants, 10 per round; 2-layer LSTM Reddit, 80,000 users, 100 per round
entries.metric: backdoor accuracy, main-task accuracy, persistence over rounds
entries.headline: single-shot single-participant attack drives backdoor accuracy near 100%; 1% attacker matches 20% data-poisoning attacker; Krum makes attack easier
entries.gaps: Attacker directly controls its update; no content-driven corruption or LLM agents.

entries.title: Byzantine-Tolerant Machine Learning
entries.attacker_access: up to f of n workers send arbitrary gradient vectors
entries.defender_assumptions: reliable trusted parameter server; synchronous rounds; i.i.d. unbiased honest gradients with bounded moments
entries.setup: theory; v1 has no experiments
entries.headline: averaging tolerates zero Byzantine workers; Krum resilient for 2f+2 < n
entries.gaps: Requires i.i.d. tightly-clustered honest contributions, which domain-diverse forks violate.

entries.title: Approximate Agreement Algorithms for Byzantine Collaborative Learning
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine clients in P2P setting make honest clients see different gradient sets
entries.defender_assumptions: no central server; approximate agreement subroutine (hyperbox)
entries.setup: centralized and decentralized experiments on non-i.i.d. data
entries.headline: geometric-median aggregation tolerates sign-flip on non-i.i.d. better than mean-based
entries.gaps: Numeric vectors; no semantic agent outputs.

entries.title: Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance
entries.attacker_access: up to floor((n-1)/3) replicas faulty; network delays
entries.defender_assumptions: independent node failures (diverse implementations, OS, admins); eventual synchrony for liveness; MACs
entries.setup: BFT NFS on Andrew benchmark
